source_uses.fact: Heritage significance derives from archaeological, architectural, artistic or historic interest and can arise from an asset’s setting as well as physical presence
LBBD identifies four conservation areas and publishes maps and guidance for them
The borough Culture and Heritage Strategy covers 2024 to 2030
Historic England provides official National Heritage List discovery for Barking and Dagenham
The current Heritage at Risk programme provides the official register and latest 2025 findings
The Old Vicarage in Dagenham is a Grade II listed Heritage at Risk entry recorded in poor condition with medium vulnerability and stable trend
Listed-building dataset is primarily point evidence and a point does not define the full affected extent or setting
Listed-building-outline data is work in progress and must not be treated as complete curtilage or setting proof
Conservation-area coverage has known incompleteness/duplicate caveats and negative results require provider-completeness checks
2026 Draft London Plan IIA consultation feedback from Historic England led to stronger landscape, townscape and heritage specificity
The new London Plan remains a draft under statutory consultation until 15 October 2026
Draft place-based policy explicitly recognises heritage and historic environment as part of place quality and green/open-space character

examples: A listed-building point does not establish the asset’s curtilage or the extent of its setting
A listed-building outline cannot by itself prove the full area of heritage effect
A conservation-area map is designation evidence but does not quantify development harm
The Old Vicarage Heritage at Risk entry is a real current constraint/context example, not a parcel-wide exclusion zone
Historic England register presence requires scheme-specific significance and impact assessment rather than a binary value haircut
A non-hit in an incomplete provider dataset cannot prove absence of heritage constraints
Draft 2026 heritage language cannot override adopted statutory policy before adoption
No promotion without exact parcel/site relation and scheme-specific heritage/archaeology assessment where relevant
